blocks.h2: Why Pipes Freeze in Hinsdale Homes
blocks.intro: A few spots in Hinsdale homes are the first to freeze.

items.body: Older houses often have little insulation where pipes run along outside walls.
Plumbing in additions built over crawl spaces is exposed to cold from below.
Lines that weren't drained in the fall split when they freeze.

blocks.h2: Burst Pipe Questions From Hinsdale Homeowners

items.q: What should I do if a pipe is frozen but not burst?
items.preview: Open the faucet and warm the pipe gently.
items.answer: Open the faucet and warm the pipe gently with a hair dryer. Never use an open flame. If you can't reach it, call us.

items.q: Can you repair a burst pipe behind plaster?
items.answer: Yes. We locate the break and open only what we need to reach it.

items.q: How do I keep pipes from freezing in a cold snap?
items.preview: Heat, open cabinets and a slow drip.
items.answer: Keep the heat on, open cabinet doors on exterior walls and let a faucet on an exterior wall drip on the coldest nights.
Often, for sudden damage. Policies vary, so check with your agent.

items.q: Our sprinkler line burst. Can you fix it?
items.preview: We fix the plumbing side up to the backflow device.
items.answer: We repair the water supply to the sprinkler system up to the backflow device. Irrigation contractors handle the zones in the yard.

items.q: How much does burst pipe repair cost in Hinsdale?
items.preview: It depends on the break. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the pipe burst and how we reach it. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
